On Mon, Aug 9, 2026 at 07:28 Soojin Lee wrote:
> Marissa / Rishi — can you triage?

Checked the deployment logs. Confirmed: hot-path pool (pool-hot-3) rolled to model redwood-llm-large-v2@v2.3.1 at 07:10 UTC. The rollout included: quantization profile Q4_8 (new packing change) and kernel KERNEL_XLA_2 which changed the fused softmax kernel.

Telemetry: starting 07:12 UTC we see a burst of 429s and 5xx (predominantly 502 gateway and 504 timeouts). Request latencies spike and then clients progressively retried causing a retry feedback loop — our own edge proxies logged a sharp increase in concurrent in-flight requests to the pool before the errors. Autoscaler did not add capacity fast enough because the requests were being rate-limited at the pool ingress.

Immediate mitigation I recommend:
- Roll pool-hot-3 back to v2.3.0 (rollback already staged).
- Throttle upstream client concurrency via the edge (apply token-bucket) to break retry feedback.
- Disable batching on pool-hot-3 during rollback to reduce per-request tail latency.

I'm initiating the rollback now and will post status.

— Rishi
Senior SW Engineer, Serving Runtime

Hi Alex / Sara,

Thanks for the sample — we can see the timestamps align to our rollout window. High-level: the incident appears tied to the kernel/quant changes in v2.3.1 on the hot GPU pool which increased variance in per-request compute time; that, combined with client retries, produced a transient overload and gateway errors.

Actions in flight (ETA in parentheses):
- Rolling pool-hot-3 back to v2.3.0 (in progress — ~5min).
- Edge token-bucket throttle to 8 concurrent per-customer token (deployed — immediate).
- Temporarily disabled batching on the hot pool (done).
- Added an automated circuit-breaker rule for >30% 5xx in 2min window to flip traffic to warm fallback pool (work item created).

We expect error rate to drop after the rollback and throttles. I'll post a follow-up when Neptune telemetry shows recovery. Apologies for the disruption — we'll do a full RCA and schedule an emergency rollback policy to avoid this during rapid kernel/profile changes.

— Marissa
Head of Production Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident summary & next steps — hot-path stall / retry feedback loop (Neptune)

Sara / Alex — quick summary and next steps now that the immediate impact window is closed.

Summary:
- Incident window: 07:12 — 09:00 UTC.
- Root cause: rollout of redwood-llm-large-v2@v2.3.1 to hot-path pool (pool-hot-3) introduced a kernel+quantization combination (KERNEL_XLA_2 + Q4_8) that increased variance and produced intermittent timeouts under Neptune's request distribution.
- Contributing factor: aggressive client retries from Neptune clients (default 3x with no exponential backoff) created a retry feedback loop that amplified load and caused ingress rate-limiting to produce 429s.

Mitigations applied:
- Immediate rollback of pool-hot-3 to v2.3.0 (completed).
- Disabled batching and conservative autoscaler profile on hot pool during rollback.
- Edge token-bucket throttle applied for per-customer concurrency.
- Temporary circuit-breaker rule added for >30% 5xx.

Impact:
- Peak 5xx/429 across Neptune traffic: 18% error-rate at peak.
- No data-loss on stored artifacts; some ephemeral requests retried client-side.

Next steps (RCA & prevention):
- Full RCA write-up (owner: Marissa) due EOD tomorrow with kernel/quant fuzz testing matrix.
- Rollout policy update (owner: Rishi): require staged canary with isolation and automatic rollback on 5xx/latency thresholds for the next 30 days.
- Client guidance (owner: Soojin & CS): recommend exponential backoff and a 30s cooldown after 5xx bursts; we'll provide a short engineers' note for Neptune to add to their SDK.
- Exec brief (owner: Soojin): one-pager for leadership with impact and risk mitigations.

Attachments: mitigation-runbook.patch, quant-profile-delta.png

If you want an immediate postmortem meeting, propose a time and we'll get the infra + product folks there.

— Soojin Lee
